hypothesis: Four warps per block cover one 32×32 input tile as 8×32 strips. Each lane first owns eight row values for its input column; four 8-lane groups then transpose their 8×8 subtiles by swapping lane/register bits with warp-local XOR shuffles. This should produce coalesced input loads and contiguous 8-float store segments without shared memory or a block barrier. The extra shuffle instructions and segmented stores may offset that benefit, so candidate timing is needed.
notes: Bit-preserving float/uint conversions carry values through integer shuffles without arithmetic. The width-8 shuffle groups lanes 0–7, 8–15, 16–23, and 24–31; the kernel uses four full warps, so every lane named by the full mask participates. No candidate build output is available here, so register count/spill status and candidate n=1024 repeated timings remain unmeasured. The supplied baseline n=1024 samples were 17.134, 16.749, and 16.875 microseconds (mean 16.919 microseconds); these are baseline evidence, not a candidate comparison.
transformations: Replace the active naive kernel launch with a 32×4-thread block; each warp loads an 8×32 strip, with all lanes loading eight rows at adjacent columns.

Transpose each 8×8 lane/register subgroup through three lane-bit/register-bit exchange stages. Each pair uses a same-warp XOR shuffle with width 8; no cross-warp exchange, shared memory, or CTA barrier is used.
Store the transposed values as eight contiguous floats per subgroup, using unsigned bit-preserving shuffles and float bitcasts for exact copies; use size_t offsets for matrix indexing.
